media_item.item_title: Book Content: Smoke But No Fire: Convicting the Innocent of Crimes That Never Happened
media_item.focus_or_theme: No-crime wrongful convictions - cases where people are convicted of crimes that never actually happened
media_item.summary_notes: The book examines the various factors contributing to no-crime wrongful convictions, from forensic errors to systemic issues within the criminal justice system. It highlights how innocent people are convicted of crimes that never occurred due to official misconduct, aggressive policing, forensic errors, false accusations, inadequate defense, and judicial bias.  Approximately one-third of all exonerations involve no-crime wrongful convictions.
media_item.case_details_raw: Rodricus Crawford's case is featured as an example of a no-crime wrongful conviction where a natural death was misclassified as murder. He was convicted of murdering his baby boy by suffocation, but the baby actually died from an undiagnosed illness.  Crawford faced a death sentence and spent years on death row before exoneration.
